data.narrative:
Halo is a Series B chip design company that has raised $122M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comparable universe of 8 private frontier-chip firms (including Positron AI, SambaNova Systems, and Rebellions) and 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $232M. Peer-median anchoring across five same-sector comparables—spanning $529M (DEEPX, Series C) to $11.0B (SambaNova, Series A)—produces a $2.0B median. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (18.4x sector median) cannot be applied due to absence of revenue disclosure. The wide peer range ($529M–$11.0B) reflects stage heterogeneity and varied technology maturity within frontier semiconductors.

Triangulation across the two applicable methods supports a valuation range of $197M–$2.3B, with a median point of $1.1B. The substantial spread reflects two key uncertainties: Halo's revenue scale and margins relative to peers remain undisclosed, and the peer set itself spans early-stage and later funding rounds with divergent risk profiles. The stage-progression floor ($232M) anchors the lower bound, while peer-median results anchor toward the $2B area. Without proprietary financial performance data, the midpoint around $1.1B represents a balanced estimate contingent on execution risk and competitive positioning.
